title: David's harp (1 Samuel 16:14–23)
hook: David plays and Saul's dark mood lifts

segments.voice: Yesterday, David, the youngest son, called in from the sheep and anointed in Bethlehem. Your line was the heart, not the height. Today, the same chapter, in the palace.

One verse says the spirit of the LORD came on David. The very next says it left Saul. And something else comes instead. The text calls it an evil spirit from the LORD, and it terrifies him. The king is in the dark, and his servants can see it. So they suggest what people still suggest for someone who's low: let us look for a man who can play the harp. When the dark comes on you, he'll play with his hand, and you'll be well. Saul says yes. Find me someone who plays well.
screen: `THE SPIRIT LEAVES SAUL.` → `THE KING IS IN THE DARK.` → `FIND SOMEONE WHO CAN PLAY.`

segments.voice: One of the young men says: I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, skillful in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent, good-looking, and the LORD is with him. So Saul sends to Jesse for David, who is with the sheep, and Jesse loads a donkey with bread, a skin of wine and a young goat, and sends his youngest son to the king. Nothing in the text says Saul knows what happened in Bethlehem, where this boy was just anointed with oil among his brothers. David walks into the palace not as a rival, but as a musician, to help the man whose throne he'll one day sit on. And the text is tender: Saul loved him greatly, and David became his armor-bearer. Let David stay with me, Saul sends word, for he has found favor in my sight. The chapter ends with a picture. Whenever the spirit from God was upon Saul, David took the harp and played with his hand, and Saul found relief, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him. The Hebrew word for this harp is kinnor, a stringed instrument. The book doesn't say what he played, or whether there were words. Just that someone played when the dark came, and the king was well. This week, a boy said speak, a mother named what was lost, a people asked for a king, a king hid and then kept the showy offering, and a shepherd was chosen for his heart. Today that shepherd sits down beside the king, and plays.
screen: `A SON OF JESSE WHO CAN PLAY.` · `THE RIVAL WALKS IN AS A HELPER.` · `SAUL LOVED HIM GREATLY.` · `THE DARK SPIRIT DEPARTED.` · then, large: `DAVID TOOK THE HARP, AND PLAYED WITH HIS HAND.`

segments.voice: Think of one person in a dark stretch right now, and one piece of music that might reach them: a song they love, a song from a better year, something quiet. Choose it, and hear a little of it in your head. If you pray, hold that person before God while you listen.
David's harp. The kinnor the young shepherd played for Saul, so that when the dark came, the king was refreshed and well.
Your line: music lifts. The rival walked in as a helper. A week in Samuel, done.

howItsDone: Jews read David's playing for Saul as part of the Former Prophets; by tradition, David is also linked with the book of Psalms.

fork.setup: you're one of Saul's servants. the king is tormented and terrified, and nothing seems to help. what do you suggest?
options: call the priests to offer a sacrifice.
find a man who plays the harp well, to play when the dark comes.
leave the king alone until it passes.
fork.reveal: they suggest a harp player, and one of them already knows a son of Jesse. when David played, Saul was refreshed, and was well.

original.note: Hebrew: kinnor, the stringed instrument David played for Saul.

what it means: the shepherd just anointed in Bethlehem walks into the palace as the king's helper, and his music lifts the king's darkness.
what a scholar hears: the spirit comes on David in one verse and leaves Saul in the next; the harp scene is built right on that turn.

chat.says: Why would David, the future king, end up playing music for Saul?
options: Saul's servants sought a harpist for his dark; David came as a helper, and it lifted.
David was sent in secretly to spy on Saul and find a way to take his throne.
Jesse sent him on his own, hoping the king would give his son a place at court.
chat.meaning: When the evil spirit troubled Saul, David played the kinnor, and Saul found relief. He came as a helper, not a rival.

kinnor.meaning: a stringed instrument; the harp David played

Jesse.meaning: David's father, who sent him with bread, wine and a goat

Bethlehem.meaning: David's hometown, where he was anointed

Saul.meaning: the king troubled by an evil spirit, whom David played for
